title: Catalog onramp: acceptance matrix + voice/play snippets (draft)
content:
Goal: produce a compact, testable acceptance matrix for new partners to go live on the cloud catalog + a small bank of voice and tile copy to A/B test during onboarding. This doc is intentionally lightweight — working notes and TODOs.

Summary:
- Problem: lots of partners hit inconsistent gating at listing time (screenshots/telemetry mismatch, region SKUs, private deployment compatibility). We need a minimal matrix to sign off quickly while protecting legal/security gates.
- Outcome: a single-page acceptance matrix (below) + 6 copy variants for tile/title/short blurb + quick experiment plan and telemetry hooks.

Acceptance matrix (single-page checklist for go/no-go):
- Billing SKU mapped and test purchase works (owner: Priya) — PASS criteria: test purchase returns 200 + invoice id.
- Tile assets: hero image 1280x720, icon 128x128, no PII (owner: Jonas).
- Technical compatibility: private deployment mode docs present + KMS integration note (owner: Ethan).
- SLA tier alignment: partner requested SLA <= enterprise baseline -> legal ok (owner: Maya).
- Security review: verified vulnerability scan report uploaded or waiver filed (owner: security reviewer).
- Region availability: required regions listed and validated against infra catalog (owner: infra eng).
- Trial provisioning: trial activation flow validated end-to-end (owner: partner success).
- Privacy & materials: copy passes legal content check (owner: legal).

Each checklist item: PASS / BLOCK / MITIGATE. "Block" requires a formal rollback plan and cannot be toggled live.

Tile and listing voice (short bank for experiments) — keep playful but professional; variants labeled A/B/C: 
- Title A: "Redwood Inference — Predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference"
- Short blurb A: "Serve embeddings and completions at predictable latency with caching, batching, and reserved capacity. Fast start: 5-minute setup."
- Title B: "High-performance LLM serving for production apps"
- Short blurb B: "Scale inference with SLA-backed capacity, private deployments, and per-route cost controls."
- Title C: "Ship LLM features faster — reliable inference platform"
- Short blurb C: "Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private modes. Built-in rollouts, observability, and cost tooling."

Longer description variations (2):
- Long 1: "Redwood Inference lets engineering teams deploy LLM-powered features with predictable latency and unit economics. Choose hosted for quick iteration, or reserve dedicated pools for steady throughput. Includes KV/prefix caching, smart routing, and observability tailored to production workloads."
- Long 2: "A production-first inference platform focusing on latency, reliability, and cost. Integrated rollouts, model variants, and a console for tracing and token-level cost analysis make it easier to keep model regressions out of user experiences."

Bullet highlights (short):
- SLA-backed dedicated pools, autoscaling
- Private deployment (VPC + on-prem) with KMS support
- Intelligent batching & prefix/KV caching
- Model catalog + versioned rollouts and fallbacks
- Token-level cost & latency visibility

Experiment plan (quick):
- Test goal: increase click-through from catalog tile to trial signup by 18% in 2 weeks.
- Variants: Title A+B+C × Blurb A+B+C (6 combos).
- Primary metric: CTA click-through rate; secondary: trial activation rate.
- Minimum experiment traffic: 500 unique impressions per variant.
- Rollout rule: top performer promoted to default tile; losers replaced.
- Measurement: use telemetry events 'catalog_impression', 'catalog_click', 'trial_activate'. Hook tickets: JIRA GTMP-1892.

Operations & infra notes (must ship before listing):
- Ensure SKU metering mapping: confirm metering dimension is tokens or requests per minute (decide by Jan 1 cutover).
- Add a smoke test that runs a warm-start inference across regions and validates tail latency (90th/99th).
- Confirm fallback model variant exists and route when dedicated capacity saturates.

Legal / compliance quick checks (for listing preflight):
- Copy claims: remove absolute promises (e.g., "zero downtime") unless SLA grantable.
- Data residency: flag partners requiring EU-only hosting (owner: compliance).
- Marketing assets: ensure logos conform to brand guidelines; include sample alt text.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Do we need separate tile copy for Private deployments? (tradeoff: clarity vs clutter)
- Trial enforcement mechanism: should we rely on cloud marketplace trial SKU or our own token-based gating?
- Should we include explicit quantization/precision details in tile copy for technical buyers?

Next actions (short):
- Priya: validate billing SKU mapping + attach purchase test case (due 2025-11-22).
- Jonas: produce hero + icon variants and upload to design folder (due 2025-11-20).
- Ethan: add smoke test + telemetry events to infra repo and open PR (linked above).
- Maya: sync with legal + compliance and finalize acceptance definitions (due 2025-11-25).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working draft; feel free to paste alternate tile copy directly into the doc and mark which JIRA ticket you tested against. If you see an acceptance criterion that should be softer (mitigation plan instead of block), annotate inline.

Attachments & references: see linked artifacts at top. Also check: confluence:GTMP-ONRAMP-45 for full onboarding playbook, and GH PR #78 for telemetry contract.

End.
